blocks.x: Cloud, Edge & Platform applied to CPG & Brands. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

CPG brands compete on shelf, on shelf-image and on data: trade spend efficiency, retail execution truth, demand signal quality and now provenance claims. The brands that win industrialize the sell-side data relationship with retailers.

items: TPM platforms resist modeling; spend decisions legacy.
Retailer portals and EDI produce a patchwork; trade-spend ROI is estimated.

Governance inherits the sector frame — EUDR among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Reliability as product: SLOs, error budgets and incident discipline that engineers actually follow.
Golden paths, paved roads: an internal platform that turns months into days.
Cost and carbon as engineering metrics: unit economics, showback and green compute by design.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Retail & Consumer Goods level this capability reads as: in-store inference for vision and personalization screens (latency local; WAN costs down). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
